title: XRP: In-Kernel Storage Functions with eBPF
summary: Lets applications ship lookup and aggregation logic as eBPF programs that run inside the NVMe driver's completion path, cutting storage-stack overhead while preserving filesystem semantics.
paper_title: XRP: In-Kernel Storage Functions with eBPF

application_domain.Storage: The system offloads storage functions and accelerates NVMe I/O operations.
application_domain.Filesystems: It propagates filesystem metadata and integrates with ext4 for logical-to-physical mapping.
application_domain.Databases: Evaluated with BPF-KV and WiredTiger storage engines.
application_domain.Operating Systems: Implements kernel modifications and new eBPF support inside Linux.

ebpf_mechanisms.kprobe: The paper introduces a custom eBPF hook in the NVMe driver interrupt/completion path; among the provided categories, kernel-level probe-style attachment is the closest match.

system_layers.Application Layer: Database and key-value store logic invokes XRP and supplies eBPF programs.
system_layers.Kernel Subsystem: Core functionality is implemented inside Linux kernel components.
system_layers.Storage Stack: The work targets and bypasses major portions of the storage stack.
system_layers.Filesystem Layer: Uses filesystem metadata digests and ext4 extent mappings.
system_layers.Hardware Interface: Hooks are placed near the NVMe device driver and hardware queues.

research_areas.Systems: Designs a complete storage data path framework.
research_areas.Operating Systems: Extends Linux kernel and eBPF infrastructure.
research_areas.Storage Systems: Focuses on storage access paths, NVMe devices, and database storage engines.
research_areas.Performance Engineering: Primary contribution is reducing latency and increasing throughput.

goals.Performance Optimization: Reduces storage-stack overhead and accelerates lookups.
goals.Scalability: Improves throughput and behavior under many threads compared with kernel bypass approaches.

deployment_type.In-Kernel: eBPF programs execute inside the kernel NVMe completion path.
deployment_type.User-Kernel Cooperative: Applications load eBPF programs and cooperate with kernel execution through read_xrp and shared context.

innovation_type.New eBPF Framework: Introduces XRP as a framework for storage-function execution using eBPF.
innovation_type.New eBPF Application: Applies eBPF to storage/data-structure traversal and database operations.
innovation_type.New eBPF System Design: Creates a new storage datapath with metadata digest, NVMe-driver hooks, and resubmission logic.

application_domain.Caching: Implements in-kernel cache for key-value lookups.
